```text
Alert me to new notifications with a tab icon badge and opt-in desktop notifications open ['enhancement', 'scope: medium'] ['CarsonRackley'] Sprint 3 CarsonRackley
Part of #7. Upstream requests: go-gitea/gitea#1415 (badge on the favicon) and go-gitea/gitea#31925 (browser notifications).

### User Story

As a user who keeps Gitea open in a background tab, I want the tab icon to show when I have unread notifications, and optionally a desktop notification when a new one arrives, so that I notice review requests and mentions without switching back to check.

### User Scenario

Marco keeps Gitea open in one of many browser tabs while he codes. On the Notifications page he clicks "Enable desktop notifications", and the browser asks for permission once. He allows it. Later a teammate requests his review. A dot appears on the Gitea tab's icon, and a desktop notification says "You have 1 new notification". He clicks it, and the browser switches to Gitea and opens his notifications. After he reads it, the unread count drops to zero and the dot disappears. When he is already looking at Gitea, no desktop notification pops up; the navbar count is enough.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: Given a signed-in user with at least one unread notification, when any Gitea page loads or the unread count updates, then the tab icon shows a badge dot, and when the count drops to 0 the default icon comes back without a reload.
- [ ] AC2: Given an Actions run page, which already sets the tab icon to the run's status, when the user also has unread notifications, then the run status icon is shown, not the notification badge.
- [ ] AC3: Given desktop notifications have never been enabled in this browser, when new notifications arrive, then no desktop notification is shown and the browser never asks for permission on its own.
- [ ] AC4: Given the user clicks "Enable desktop notifications" on the Notifications page, when the browser asks for permission and the user denies it, then the page says notifications are blocked by the browser and the setting stays off.
- [ ] AC5: Given desktop notifications are enabled and permission is granted, when the unread count goes up while the Gitea tab is hidden, then exactly one desktop notification is shown saying how many new notifications there are, without the issue title or repository name.
- [ ] AC6: Given Gitea is open in several tabs, when the unread count goes up, then the user gets one desktop notification, not one per tab.
- [ ] AC7: Given the Gitea tab is visible, or the count stays the same or goes down, when the count updates, then no desktop notification is shown.
- [ ] AC8: Given a desktop notification is shown, when the user clicks it, then the browser focuses Gitea and opens `/notifications`.
- [ ] AC9: Given desktop notifications are enabled, when the user clicks "Disable desktop notifications", then no more desktop notifications are shown in that browser.

### Out of Scope

- Notifications when no Gitea tab is open (Web Push with a service worker and server-side keys).
- A number inside the badge, or a count in the page title.
- Per-type or per-repository rules for which notifications alert.
- Sounds, email, and the mobile or API side of notifications.

### Open Questions

- Should the badge be something the user can turn off? (Proposed: no. It is passive and only appears when there is something unread.)
- Should the alert also fire when the page falls back to polling because the event stream is unavailable? (Proposed: yes, both update paths behave the same.)

### Design Decisions

#### Decision 1: The desktop notification opt-in is stored per browser, not on the account

**Decision:** "Enable desktop notifications" is remembered in the browser's local storage.
**Alternatives Considered:** (a) A per-user setting stored on the server, shown in Settings. (b) No stored setting: alert whenever the browser permission is granted.
**Rationale:** Browser permission is per browser and per device anyway, and browsers only allow the permission prompt after a click. A server-side setting would turn on in a browser that never granted permission and would have to prompt without a click, which browsers block. With (b), users who granted permission for something else could not turn the alerts off without revoking it.
**Consequences:** No server or schema change. The choice does not follow the user to other browsers, and clearing site data turns it off.

#### Decision 2: The desktop notification shows only a count

**Decision:** The notification text is "You have N new notifications" and clicking it opens `/notifications`.
**Alternatives Considered:** (a) Show the newest notification's issue title and repository. (b) Show one notification per new item, each linking to its issue.
**Rationale:** The live update only delivers a count, so (a) and (b) need an extra API request per update. Titles from private repositories would also appear on a lock screen or a shared screen. A count is enough to make the user switch tabs.
**Consequences:** The user cannot tell a review request from a subscription update until they open Gitea. Richer content is follow-up work if users ask for it.

#### Decision 3: Badge as a dot, with Actions run status taking precedence

**Decision:** The badge is a plain dot drawn on the Gitea icon, reusing the drawing code that already badges the icon with an Actions run's status. On a run page the run status wins.
**Alternatives Considered:** (a) Draw the unread number in the icon. (b) Put the count in the page title, like "(3) Gitea".
**Rationale:** A number is unreadable at 16 px and needs a "9+" cap. The title is truncated in a crowded tab bar and changes the text screen readers announce. On a run page the user is watching that run, so its status is the more useful icon.
**Consequences:** The icon code needs to know which badge currently owns the icon, so leaving a run page or reading every notification restores the right one.

### Scope

medium
```

```text
55	async function updateNotificationCountWithCallback(callback: (timeout: number, newCount: number) => void, timeout: number, lastCount: number) {
```

```markdown
# Issue #118 — spec review comment

## Comment 1: spec review

Spec reviewed (Sprint 3 re-check) — ready to implement once the five required points below are settled in the issue body. My Sprint 2 approval was a one-line comment, so this replaces it with a detailed check now that the issue is being picked up.

I checked the spec against `web_src/js/features/notification.ts`, `web_src/js/eventsource.sharedworker.ts`, `web_src/js/modules/favicon-status.ts` and its test, `web_src/js/components/RepoActionView.vue`, `modules/eventsource/manager_run.go`, `GetUIDsAndNotificationCounts` in `models/activities/notification.go`, `templates/base/head.tmpl`, `templates/base/head_navbar_icons.tmpl`, `templates/base/head_script.tmpl` and `tests/e2e/events.test.ts`, all on `main` (1942a0cba6).

**Format: passes.** The story meets INVEST and the scenario is concrete. There are 9 ACs, each with a clear pass/fail result, plus Out of Scope and Open Questions. All three decisions name two concrete alternatives and say why each lost. Decision 2's privacy argument (titles from private repositories on a lock screen) is a good one. The issue has `scope: medium` and one assignee. It still needs to go on the Sprint 3 milestone, as the deferral comment says.

**Required**

1. **AC5–AC7: say what "the Gitea tab is visible" means when there are several tabs.** In the event-stream path the shared worker sends every `notification-count` event to every open tab (`eventsource.sharedworker.ts:58-61`). In the polling path each tab polls on its own. If each tab checks only its own `document.hidden`, Marco can be looking at one Gitea tab while a second, hidden Gitea tab still pops a desktop notification. That breaks the scenario's last sentence. Pick a rule and write it into AC7, for example "no desktop notification while **any** Gitea tab in this browser is visible". Add a line under a decision on how tabs agree: tabs report visibility to the shared worker, or a `BroadcastChannel` with one tab in charge. For AC6, also name the dedupe method. A shared `tag` on the `Notification` makes the browser replace instead of stack, but it does not stop the visible-tab case above.
2. **AC5/AC7: a second comment on an already-unread thread will never alert.** The server sends the user's *total unread count* (`GetUIDsAndNotificationCounts`, `notification.go:378`). Gitea keeps one notification per issue, so a new comment on an issue that is already unread re-sends the same count. Under "count goes up" that gives no desktop notification. That may be the right call, but the spec should say so. Add it to Out of Scope or Decision 2's consequences ("only new unread threads alert, not more activity on a thread that is already unread"), so the tester doesn't file it as a bug.
3. **Define what the count is compared against.** `receiveUpdateCount` (`notification.ts:8`) overwrites `.notification_count` without keeping the old value. `updateNotificationCount` returns `0` when a fetch fails (`notification.ts:124`). If the "previous count" is the last value a function returned, a network blip followed by a good poll looks like a jump from 0 to N and fires a false alert. AC7 should say the baseline is the count shown before this update, and that failed fetches are ignored. Also state that a page load never alerts by itself. Otherwise a navigation where the server-rendered count is higher than on the last page is unclear.
4. **The browser may not offer notifications at all.** The Notifications API works only in a secure context (HTTPS or localhost), and some browsers don't support it. Many self-hosted Gitea instances run on plain HTTP. Add an AC: "Given the browser can't show notifications (no `Notification` API or not a secure context), the Enable button is hidden or disabled with a short reason". Also cover permission that is **already** `denied` when the page loads, and a prompt the user closes without choosing (`default`). AC4 covers only a denial during the prompt.
5. **Say where the translated notification text comes from.** The desktop notification can fire from any page, but `head_script.tmpl:20` says the global `window.config.i18n` "should only contain general texts", and the Notifications page's data attributes exist only on that page. Decision 2 should name the source of the singular/plural text, for example a small entry added to `window.config.notificationSettings` or a reasoned exception to the i18n rule. Otherwise the implementer will hard-code English.

**Optional**

6. **Make Decision 3's consequence into an AC.** `favicon-status.ts` assumes it owns the icon. `resetActionFavicon` (`favicon-status.ts:83`) restores the original `<link>` hrefs, and `RepoActionView.vue:123-128` calls it when the run status is cleared or the view unmounts. Suggested AC: "Given unread notifications and a run page whose status badge is cleared, the notification dot comes back, and a notification count update never replaces a run status icon". It also helps to say both badges go through one owner/priority function in `favicon-status.ts` rather than two modules writing `link.href`.
7. **Close the open questions.** Q2: yes. Both paths already meet in the same `.notification_count` update, so one hook covers both. Q1: agreed, no toggle. Moving both answers into the body makes the spec final.
8. **Test plan.** `tests/e2e/events.test.ts` already has a "notification count" test that creates a notification through the API. AC1 (dot appears and clears) can extend it. For AC5–AC9, Vitest with a stubbed `Notification` and `document.visibilityState` is quicker and more reliable than real OS notifications. Note in the issue which ACs are covered where.
9. **Shared computers.** Decision 1 stores the opt-in per browser, not per user. If another account later signs in on the same browser it inherits the opt-in, though it still needs the browser permission. Either key the stored value by user ID or note this under Consequences.
```

The spec review for #118 is drafted in [issue-118-spec-review-draft.md](docs/sprint3/issue-118-spec-review-draft.md). I checked every file and line it mentions against `origin/main` (1942a0cba6). Nothing is posted to GitHub and nothing is committed.

You already approved this spec in Sprint 2 with a one-line comment. Carson deferred the issue to Sprint 3, so the draft is written as a detailed re-check that replaces that approval.

**Required points:**
1. **Several open tabs:** the shared worker sends the count update to every tab, and in the polling fallback each tab polls on its own. If each tab only checks whether it is hidden itself, a background Gitea tab will pop a desktop notification while Marco is looking at another Gitea tab. The spec needs a rule for this and a way for tabs to agree.
2. **New activity on an issue that's already unread never alerts:** the server sends the total unread count, and Gitea keeps one notification per issue, so the count doesn't go up. The spec should say whether that's intended.
3. **What "the count went up" is measured against:** a failed poll returns `0` (`notification.ts:124`). If an implementation compares against that, a network blip followed by a good poll looks like a jump from 0 to N and fires a false alert. The spec should also say that a page load never alerts by itself.
4. **Browsers that can't show notifications:** browsers only allow them over HTTPS or on localhost, and many self-hosted Gitea instances run on plain HTTP. AC4 also doesn't cover permission that was already denied before the page loaded.
5. **Where the translated text comes from:** the notification can fire from any page, but `head_script.tmpl:20` says the global translation object is only for general texts. Without a decision the implementer will likely hard-code English.

**Optional points:** turn Decision 3's tab-icon handover into an AC, settle the two open questions, add a test plan that builds on the existing `events.test.ts` e2e test, and decide what happens when two accounts share one browser.
